ui.settings.tip.notices: Shows a short message after every operation, whether it succeeded or failed. When off, a failed operation shows nothing; loading errors are still shown on the screen. Default: on.
ui.settings.tip.menuRefresh: Seconds between automatic refreshes of the numbers in the main menu. 0 turns the timed refresh off, otherwise a whole number from 5 to 3600. Defaults: {normal} seconds, and {busy} seconds while AI tasks wait. The numbers also refresh when you return to the window. The choices above them say which numbers each menu item shows: one, or two shown as "first / second". The badge is hidden when every chosen number is 0; a 0 next to a non-zero number is shown.
ui.settings.tip.setup: Creates or updates the folder, the spreadsheet, its sheets and the hourly trigger. Run it after every update of the app. It is safe to run again: it never overwrites your data.
ui.settings.tip.documents: Which documents are created and handed to the AI when you prepare an application: resume, cover letter and other. Default: resume and cover letter.
ui.settings.tip.experience: Your experience, skills, projects and what you look for, in as much detail as you like. The AI uses it as the only source of facts about you when it evaluates a job and writes documents. At most {max} characters. Every save is kept as a version: use the History button to read, comment, pin or restore earlier versions.
ui.settings.tip.prompts: The whole text sent to the AI as a task. It is copied when the task is created, so a change applies only to new tasks. Placeholders in double braces are filled in at that moment. A prompt cannot be empty and has at most {max} characters. Reset all to default brings back the built-in texts.
ui.settings.tip.availability: Switches the regular check on and sets the hours of the day (0 to 23, separated by commas, in the time zone {zone}) when the app visits saved ads and marks the ones that disappeared as offline. Reasons that are ticked mark an ad offline at once; the others need two checks in a row. The offline texts are phrases that mean the ad is gone, one per line. Default: off, hour 18.
ui.settings.tip.profileLinks: Your contact links for the templates: Portfolio, LinkedIn, GitHub and your personal website each have their own placeholder (portfolio, linkedin, github and website in double braces). The links placeholder lists all the filled links together, one per line, followed by the other links.
ui.settings.tip.templates: A template is a Google Doc with placeholders in double braces. Choose its type (resume, cover letter or other), a language (empty means any) and paste the address of the Doc. New documents are copies of it.
ui.settings.tip.jobStatuses: The statuses of saved ads: their names, colours and whether the regular availability check visits ads in that status. The built-in statuses cannot be deleted; your own can be deleted when no ad uses them.
ui.settings.tip.statusLabels: The text (at most {max} characters, empty means the default) and the colour (a hex colour such as #2563eb) of each application status. The tick says whether the availability check visits ads that have an application in that status.
ui.settings.tip.transitions: Tick which status an application may move to. It applies everywhere: the status control of an application and the Kanban board. Moving to Waiting always asks for a reminder date.

ui.help.jobs.i21: When the app cannot download an ad (for example LinkedIn answers HTTP 429), Add job offers to paste the text. The checkbox "Create AI job to import" under the link is always there, so you can also tick it before reading the ad, for instance when a site shows its ad text only in the browser and the app finds just a title (it is off while text is pasted, and needs your experience described in Settings). Below it you can write extra instructions for the AI (optional), for example where in the ad to look for something; they are added to the task. "Create AI job" then saves a placeholder job and queues one AI task that reads the ad, fills in the job and evaluates your match in one go; tell Claude: run the pending tasks. Its prompt is the tab "Import + match" in Settings > AI prompts ("Reset all to default" brings the new one to an existing installation). If a site blocks the AI (HTTP 429, a login wall), the prompt tells it to try the one address once in your own browser through the Chrome extension, where you are signed in, and to stop at any further obstacle.

ui.help.title: Help
ui.help.how.title: How it works
ui.help.how.intro: JobHunters is a personal tool that keeps your whole job search in one place. Your data lives in your own Google Sheet and Google Drive. The typical flow:
ui.help.how.i1: Add a job: by its link, by pasting the text of the ad, or many links at once. When the app cannot read a link, paste the text or let the AI import the ad and evaluate the match.
ui.help.how.i2: Check the ad: its status, whether it is still online and how well the AI thinks it matches you (a percentage).
ui.help.how.i3: Create an application: its documents are made from your templates and can be written by the AI (you tell your AI assistant, for example Claude, to "run the pending tasks" afterwards).
ui.help.how.i4: Answer the questions of the application, if it has any.
ui.help.how.i5: Send it and track the status of the application.
ui.help.how.i6: Note the communication and use reminders, then follow up until the result.
ui.help.dashboard.title: Dashboard
ui.help.dashboard.intro: The first screen shows what needs your attention.
ui.help.dashboard.i1: Open reminders (overdue, today, soon): mark one as done, postpone it, or open its application.
ui.help.dashboard.i2: The number of applications in each status; a click opens the list filtered by that status.
ui.help.dashboard.i3: A button to add a new job.
ui.help.dashboard.i4: The card "AI tasks waiting" shows how many AI tasks wait for Claude, by type.
ui.help.jobs.title: Jobs
ui.help.jobs.intro: All the ads you have collected.
ui.help.jobs.i1: The list has a search box (it looks in the title, the company, the place and the work mode: type Remote or Hybrid), filters by the availability and by the ad status, a checkbox "Hide No" that hides the jobs you set to No (it is remembered, like the one that hides jobs with an application), and a checkbox that shows only gigs.
ui.help.jobs.i2: Add a job by its link or by pasting the text of the ad. Add job opens as a pop-up; the green plus next to Jobs in the main menu opens it from any screen.
ui.help.jobs.i3: A job opens as a pop-up over the list. Its tabs are Applications, Notes, Description and Match.
ui.help.jobs.i4: Ad statuses: New, No, Awaiting AI (set by the app for ads it handed to the AI; it cannot be chosen by hand) and your own (edit them in Settings). The regular availability check visits ads without an application and ads with an application in a status that has "Check availability" ticked.
ui.help.jobs.i5: The Availability button checks at once whether the ad is still online; a regular check does it by itself in the hours you choose.
ui.help.jobs.i6: The Match tab asks the AI whether you suit the role; a new ad then shows the match as a coloured percentage.
ui.help.jobs.i7: You can mark an ad as a gig.
ui.help.jobs.i8: The "Several links" tab of Add job takes many links at once, one per line. Each ad is saved by itself and the result of every link is listed. While it works you see which ad out of how many is being processed, with a progress bar and the link being read; the Stop button ends the work. When it ends, a green block (orange when something was not saved) says what happened, with the buttons Close (closes the whole window), AI tasks (for ads sent to the AI) and Add more.
ui.help.jobs.i9: A link the app cannot read (LinkedIn, for example) becomes a job with the status "Awaiting AI" and an AI task. Once the AI has read it, the job becomes a normal ad.
ui.help.jobs.i10: A job that is awaiting the AI can be deleted like any job without an application; removing its AI task deletes it too.
ui.help.jobs.i11: Each job in the list is a card with a narrow column of icons on the right: open the original ad, check its availability and, for a job without an application, delete it.
ui.help.jobs.i12: A job with no match and no application has the checkbox "Evaluate my match with AI" at the bottom right of the card. It is disabled until you describe your experience in Settings.
ui.help.jobs.i13: The numbers in the main menu: by default Jobs shows the count of new jobs (status New), Applications the count of drafts and AI tasks the count of waiting tasks. In Settings, General, card Menu numbers you choose for each of the three items one number or two (shown as first / second): for Jobs for example new jobs with no application. Point at a number to read what it means. A badge is hidden when every chosen number is zero (a 0 next to a non-zero number is shown); on a small screen it is a badge on the icon.
ui.help.jobs.i14: Hover tooltips: the menu numbers, the green plus and the icons on a job card (open the ad, check availability, delete) show what they are when you point at them.
ui.help.jobs.i15: The "Sort by" dropdown orders the list: newest first (the default), oldest first, best match first or worst match first. Jobs without a match always come last when sorting by match.
ui.help.jobs.i16: The checkbox "Hide jobs with an application" removes the jobs you have already applied to from the list. Both choices are remembered between visits.
ui.help.jobs.i17: The button "Clear filters" appears at the end of the filter bar as soon as any filter is on (search, availability, status, gig, hiding jobs with an application or hiding jobs with the status No). It resets the filters but keeps the sort order.
ui.help.jobs.i18: A job without an application also has the checkbox "Prepare with AI" in the narrow column of the card. Ticking it at once creates the application, makes the documents of your default set (resume and cover letter) in the language of the ad (English or Czech, otherwise your default document language) and queues one AI task for each. The box then disappears from the card; tell Claude: run the pending tasks. It is disabled until you describe your experience in Settings.
ui.help.jobs.i19: The card and the detail of a job show the type of employment and the salary of the ad. The checkboxes Remote and Hybrid (both can be ticked) are always shown in the detail of a job and in the detail of an application, and a click is saved at once; you can also tick them in the review form of Add job, next to Gig. Portals that state a work mode tick them for you, and the card lists the ticked ones. "Refresh the ad" never changes them. When the AI has estimated a salary (when it evaluates your match or writes a resume or cover letter), it is shown too, marked as an AI estimate: what to ask for and the realistic range per month. The estimate is written to the Jobs sheet only once and never overwritten.
ui.help.jobs.i20: In the detail, the button "Application" (with the plus) sits on the right of the title. Under the title the summary has two columns: the details of the ad on the left and a narrow column on the right with the status drop-down above a grid of icon buttons, four or five (the fifth, the trash, only for a job without an application; on a phone this column comes first). Hover an icon to see what it does: the circular arrow "Refresh the ad" downloads the ad again and overwrites what was read from it (title, location, salary, type, dates, description, language) while your notes, status, gig flag, Remote and Hybrid boxes, match, AI salary estimate and the saved copy of the page stay; the check mark checks whether the ad is still online; the arrow out of a box opens the ad on its website; the folder opens the ad's folder in Google Drive; the trash deletes the job (only for a job without an application). Jobs waiting for the AI have only the link to the ad.
ui.help.applications.title: Applications
ui.help.applications.intro: Your applications, as a list or as a Kanban board.
ui.help.applications.i1: The status filter is a multiple choice. The list and the board remember their own selection.
ui.help.applications.i2: Kanban: a column per status. Drag a card to another column to change its status, or within a column to change its order. On a touch screen use the "Move to…" menu of the card.
ui.help.applications.i3: "Hide empty columns" hides the columns without applications.
ui.help.applications.i4: An application opens as a pop-up over the list. Tabs: Ad (the saved text of the ad, opened first), Documents (preview, PDF export, "Content by AI"), Questions ("Answer by AI" with a maximum number of sentences), Communication (messages, meetings, homework and confirmations), Reminders and Timeline.
ui.help.applications.i5: The status control offers only the changes allowed in Settings. Moving to Waiting asks for a reminder date.
ui.help.applications.i6: The exported PDF is named "Your name – Document type – Company – Job title"; your name comes from Settings → Profile. "Export PDF" saves it into the folder of the application; exporting again replaces that same file, so there is always only one. "Download PDF" saves it to your computer with one click, from Drive, without opening a tab of its own.
ui.help.applications.i7: The search box looks in the label of the application, the title and company of the job, its place and its work mode (Remote or Hybrid). The button "Clear filters" appears when the search or a status selection is on. It clears both for the list or the board you are looking at; the Kanban switch and "Hide empty columns" stay as they are.
ui.help.applications.i8: By default the number next to "Applications" in the main menu is how many applications are still in draft. You can choose another one in Settings (drafts, waiting for a reply, sent, all active).
ui.help.companies.title: Companies
ui.help.companies.i1: A list of companies with a search box and a detail with the website, notes and the jobs and applications of the company.
ui.help.tasks.title: AI tasks
ui.help.tasks.intro: Everything you ask the AI to do is queued as a task. Tasks wait until you tell Claude to "run the pending tasks"; the AI does not work by itself.
ui.help.tasks.i1: The list shows each task with its state (waiting, in progress, done, needs input, failed) and its result.
ui.help.tasks.i2: A task that is stuck can be removed.
ui.help.tasks.i3: Job import (and match): when you tell Claude to "run the pending tasks", the AI reads the pages of awaiting jobs carefully, one page at a time, fills in the job and, for "Job import and match", evaluates how well you match it. It stops at any block (a login wall or a robot check); such a task then needs your input.
ui.help.tasks.i4: By default the number next to AI tasks in the main menu is the count of waiting tasks (waiting or in progress); it is hidden when there are none. In Settings you can show instead, or besides, the tasks that need your answer or the failed ones.
ui.help.settings.title: Settings
ui.help.settings.i1: General: small cards in a grid: language, colour mode, Notices (the switch for the short notice after an operation finishes), Menu numbers (which numbers each menu item shows, one or two, and how often they refresh, in seconds; 0 turns the timed refresh off) and Setup (the button runs setup: it creates or updates the folder, the spreadsheet, its sheets and the hourly trigger, and shows what it did in a window; run it after every update; it never overwrites your data).
ui.help.settings.i2: Documents: where and how the documents are created.
ui.help.settings.i3: Experience: your experience, which the AI uses.
ui.help.settings.i4: AI prompts: the full text of every AI task on its own tab, including "Importing a job ad from a link", with a button to reset them all. The new prompt is there by default; "Reset all to default" restores it.
ui.help.settings.i5: Availability: the regular check of ads, its hours and the reasons that mark an ad offline.
ui.help.settings.i6: Profile: your personal data for the documents, with separate Portfolio, LinkedIn, GitHub and Personal website links. Each has its own placeholder in templates (portfolio, linkedin, github and website in double braces); the links placeholder lists all of them together, one per line, followed by the other links.
ui.help.settings.i7: Templates: the templates of the documents.
ui.help.settings.i8: Statuses: one tab with two sub-tabs. "Ad (job) statuses": your own statuses of ads, with a check of availability. "Application statuses": two tabs, "Labels and colours" (the names and colours of the application statuses) and "Allowed changes" (which status an application may move to).
ui.help.settings.i9: The question-mark icon next to a setting explains what it sets and the allowed values. Hover it to see the text, or click or tap it to read it in a window.
ui.help.settings.i10: Setup button: Settings, tab General. The window shows the verdict (OK or failed) and every step setup did. A red exclamation mark by Settings in the menu, on the tab and on the card means something needs you: setup has something left to create (the card lists it), or the built-in AI prompts changed in a new version (tab AI prompts: press "Reset all to default" to take the new texts, which replaces your own edits, or "Keep my prompts" to hide the notice). The mark disappears when you have done it.
ui.help.settings.i11: About: the version and the switch that shows element IDs.
ui.help.settings.i12: History of texts: the button History (N) sits next to Save on the Experience tab, under the text of every AI prompt (the one on the open tab, each prompt has a history of its own) and next to the offline texts on the tab Availability. Every saved change of such a text is kept as a version; "Reset all to default" of the prompts is kept too, so your own prompts can always be brought back. In the window you pick a version on the left; the Changes tab on the right compares it with the current text (red disappears from the current text, green appears when you use the version, changed words are marked), and the Text tab shows the whole text. A version can have a comment and a pin. Use This restores a version after a confirmation, as a new version, so nothing is lost; Delete removes an unpinned version. Pinned versions and the first one are not counted and never deleted. Tab General has the limit of unpinned versions (default 50); when it is reached, saving is refused until you delete some.
ui.help.tips.title: Tips
ui.help.tips.i1: Alt+Shift+I shows the IDs of elements (the same switch is in Settings); it helps when you want to point at something.
ui.help.tips.i2: All times are shown in the time zone of the script.
ui.help.tips.i3: The choice between the list and the Kanban board and the filters of the applications are remembered.
ui.help.tips.i4: Your data lives in the Google Sheet, so you can also look at it there.

ui.deleteJob.title: Delete job
ui.deleteJob.text: "{title}" will be deleted together with its AI tasks. This cannot be undone.

ui.deleteJob.trashHint: Only when it holds nothing but saved ads and no other job uses it. You can restore it from the Drive trash.

ui.help.jobs.i25: Ad statuses Applied and Archived: when you create an application for a job that is New, the job becomes Applied; when an application moves to Rejected, its job becomes Archived (a job with the status No or one of your own statuses stays as it is). Applying again for an archived job makes it Applied again. Nothing moves back by itself: set a job to New by hand when you want it there. The count of new jobs in the menu counts only jobs that are really New. The first time you run Setup after the update it moves the jobs that already have an application from New to Applied (Archived when their latest application is rejected).
ui.help.jobs.i26: Link of a job: a job without a link (for example an imported one) shows a red icon in place of the icon that opens the ad, on its card, in its detail and in the detail of its application. Click it to add the link; a link that is not a web address, or that another job already has, is refused. Refresh and the availability check need a link, so they are off until you add one. In the detail of a job the field Link shows the address and a double-click changes it.
ui.help.jobs.i24: Contact person and reason why not: the detail of a job (and of its application) has a field Contact person, the person the ad names as responsible for the position or as a contact; the AI fills it when it evaluates your match or imports the ad, and you can change it by a double-click. When you set the status of a job to No, the field Reason why not opens at once so you can write why (Esc skips it); it stays visible while it has text and can be changed by a double-click.
ui.help.jobs.i23: Deleting a job: a job that has no application can be deleted with the trash icon on its card, or under the status in its detail; a job with an application cannot (delete the application first). The window offers to move the folder with the saved ad to the Drive trash; that happens only when the folder holds nothing but saved ads and no other job uses it, otherwise the folder stays and a notice says why. Companies are not deleted.
